question.text: Research by Rosenberg, Reid and Lanstein (1985) and subsequent studies established the 'Value Anomaly'. Which relationship is at the heart of this anomaly?

answer.text: High P/E ratio stocks have systematically outperformed low P/E stocks.
Stocks with low dividend yield outperform those with high dividend yield over long horizons.
A POSITIVE relationship between book-value-to-price (BV/P) ratio and future returns - stocks with high BV/P have generated superior risk-adjusted returns.
Growth stocks consistently beat value stocks across all developed markets.

explanation.text: The Logic: The value anomaly is a positive relationship between the book-value-to-price (BV/P) ratio and future returns: high BV/P stocks have generated superior risk-adjusted returns. The Trap: Options A and D reverse the value/growth relationship; Option B misstates the dividend-yield finding. Only the BV/P framing captures the documented anomaly. Note: Source page 51 of FINAL Series XIX-C AIF Managers (Dec 2025) workbook.
